title: Short Stature and Growth Failure: GHD Auxology, Provocative Tests and Pituitary MRI
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Thyroid Disorders, Short Stature and Skeletal Dysplasias

steps.say: Auxological assessment defines short stature and abnormal velocity thresholds across pediatric growth curves.
steps.tx: Evaluate linear auxology by comparing **Short stature statistical definitions** against established population reference charts. Short stature is defined as height > 2 standard deviations below the mean for age and sex (height SDS < -2.0, or < 3rd percentile); growth failure is annual height velocity < 25th percentile for age over 6-12 months.

vis.title: Auxological Criteria for Growth Evaluation
rows: Meets definition of short stature (< 3rd percentile)

steps.say: Target height calculation identifies whether a child is growing within their genetic family expectation.
steps.tx: Calculate genetic growth expectations using **Mid-parental height target calculation** formulas adjusted for sex. Target height calculation: For boys = [Father height + Mother height + 13 cm] / 2; For girls = [Father height - 13 cm + Mother height] / 2; target range is ± 8.5 cm (± 2 SD).

right.title: Target Height for Girls
points: Guides pathological workup when outside range

steps.say: Stable circulating binding proteins provide dependable screening markers that overcome natural pulsatile peaks.
steps.tx: Screen suspected growth hormone axis deficiency using **IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 screening** assays from peripheral serum. Serum IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 reflect integrated GH secretion; levels < -2 SD for age and pubertal stage support GH deficiency or GH insensitivity, unaffected by pulsatility.

vis.title: Serum Biomarkers for Somatotropic Axis
rows: < -2 SD for age and pubertal stage
High sensitivity in children < 3 years old
Misleading due to pulsatile ultradian spikes

steps.say: Confirmation of deficiency requires documented subnormal peaks across two independent stimulation challenges.
steps.tx: Establish definitive biochemical failure by meeting **Provocative GH testing criteria** using standardized pharmacologic triggers. Definitive diagnosis of GHD requires failure to reach peak GH >= 7-10 ng/mL on two separate provocative stimulation tests (clonidine, arginine, glucagon, or insulin tolerance test).

nodes.label: Confirmed Diagnosis of Growth Hormone Deficiency

steps.say: Exogenous sex steroids must be administered before provocative testing in peri-pubertal children.
steps.tx: Prevent false diagnostic categorization by implementing **Sex-steroid priming before GH testing** in mature children. Pre-pubertal boys > 10 years and girls > 9 years with delayed bone age require sex-steroid priming (intramuscular testosterone or oral estradiol) prior to GH testing to prevent false-positive subnormal peaks.

right.title: Priming in Girls (> 9 years)
points: Oral estradiol given prior to testing protocol

steps.say: High resolution neuroimaging reveals pathognomonic anatomic anomalies of the pituitary stalk and gland.
steps.tx: Delineate midline cranial structural architecture by assessing **Pituitary MRI findings in congenital GHD** on magnetic resonance scans. Brain MRI evaluates the hypothalamic-pituitary axis; the triad of pituitary stalk interruption syndrome consists of ectopic posterior pituitary bright spot, hypoplastic/absent infundibulum, and anterior pituitary hypoplasia.

nodes.label: Ectopic Posterior Pituitary Bright Spot at Tuber Cinereum
Severe Anterior Pituitary Hypoplasia in Sella

steps.say: Daily bedtime subcutaneous injections provide physiological hormone replacement titrated to circulating biomarkers.
steps.tx: Restore physiologic catch-up velocity by calculating **Recombinant human growth hormone dosing** based on body mass. Somatropin is initiated at 0.16-0.24 mg/kg/week (divided into daily subcutaneous bedtime injections), monitoring linear growth and titrating dose to maintain serum IGF-1 between 0 and +2 SDS.

vis.title: Somatropin Therapy and Dose Titration
rows: Divided into 6-7 daily bedtime subcutaneous injections
Titrate dose every 3-6 months to avoid overdose
Maximal catch-up growth seen in year 1 of therapy

steps.say: Routine clinical surveillance detects orthopedic and intracranial adverse effects during rapid linear growth acceleration.
steps.tx: Safeguard musculoskeletal and metabolic health through meticulous **Safety monitoring during GH therapy** throughout childhood. Children on GH must be monitored for slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE, limping or knee pain), idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri, headache/vomiting), scoliosis progression, and hyperglycemia.
